newsitem.title: USA: Cargill sets downtime for two U.S. crushing plants.
newsitem.headline: Cargill sets downtime for two U.S. crushing plants.

text.p: Cargill Inc will temporarily close its Kansas City and Norfolk, Va. soybean crushing plants, a Cargill spokeswoman said.
Cargill's crushing plant at Norfolk will close on April 1, and its facility in Kansas City will be closed May 1 through the end of August, according to spokeswoman Peggy Weller.
Information on when the Norfolk facility will re-open was not available, Weller said.
Although Weller could not specify why the plants will be closed, other sources at Cargill cited poor crushing margins.
The Norfolk crushing plant is typically closed during the summer months, but downtime is usually not taken this early during the year, a Cargill source said.
Cargill recently closed its Guntersville, Ala. crushing facility because flooding along the Ohio River had made securing soybeans difficult. That plant will be closed from March 12 through the 27th.
Other U.S. crushers were said to be slowing the pace of soymeal and soyoil production.
